pages.transcription:
New York, 10. 4. 41

Dear Hanna & Manfred,
This morning your letter (March 25th!) arrived and a few hours
later Eva & two great pleasures one day. She has grown
quite a lot in those weeks at Croton, is her old self, gay
and lively and I believe glad to be with us. I have
just put her to bed after bathing her - at her own request -
and she is really growing from a child into a girl, even
showing faint traces of developing a bosom. We will have her
photographed for you next week and I think you will find
her a little thinner, although still well filled out, and
the face not more quite so round. I shall have to get her
one or two more summerdresses (the ones she brought over will
be lengthened by a little dressmaker) and a few pairs of
socks, otherwise she seems to have all she needs. Although
while she found it very nice at Salmon's (I am sure she never
was unhappy there) she feels absolutely at home in Amity Hall
and has a great love for Mrs. Sch. I think you took the
big words in her letter to you too seriously. She has de-
finitely been influenced by Frend, but what she has
taken over is only the friendly understanding and the big
words. In her education method she is as normal and healthy
as you could wish and I believe, if you could see her you
would find yourself in complete agreement about the up-
bringing of children. As to her or their own children, I know
the three small ones, very nice fair and blue-eyed, perfectly
normal children, and Marilis, the 20 year old girl who is
looking after the children and who has graduated in
astronomical mathematics!) a very pleasant girl. One boy is
in college, apparently working his way through. And one, a big
boy, from Mr. Sch's first marriage, is not quite normal and
they had to leave him behind. Mr. Sch. himself does not
seem to have an agreable temper, but as he has nothing
to do with the education and seldom sees the children
except at mealtime, he is without importance as far as I can see.
I would have more to write, but
Stefan wants to send the letter off. So best love and
keep well
Lotte
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief in violetter Tinte. Sehr gut lesbar.
Rückseite des Dokuments, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through). Gemäß Anweisung nicht transkribiert.
Farbskala/Grauskala für Archivierung. Überdeckt einen Teil des Brieftextes.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr deutlich geschrieben und weist kaum Unklarheiten auf. Die Überlagerung durch die Farbskala auf Seite 3 beeinträchtigt die Lesbarkeit des Originals nicht, da der Text auf Seite 1 vollständig vorliegt.
